The bandpass centre frequency is the failing spec: it simulates at 26.6 MHz against a 25.2–30.8 Hz target, a factor of about 10⁶ too high. Gain, power, and the DC output level are all plausible, so the fault is most likely in the filter's frequency-setting network rather than the amplifier.

For this MFB-style bandpass, the centre frequency depends on the R·C products in the feedback network. The lowest-frequency time constant is set by the series R3–C2 branch, so an exponent slip of 10⁶ in C2 (about 7.9e-13 F written where roughly 7.9e-7 F was intended) would move f0 from tens of MHz to tens of Hz. C1 enters through a square root, so a single 10⁶ error there would only shift f0 by about 10³, which doesn't fit the observed ratio. R3 is the next most sensitive element in the same branch.

I'm not fully certain of this. As written, all the filter capacitors are in the sub-pF range, so the nominal design may also sit in the MHz range, which would point to a broader scaling problem than one corrupted element. I'd check this by simulating the netlist with C2 scaled by 10⁶ and confirming f0 lands near 28 Hz with the other specs intact.
